reply_text:
I found two dated predictions from Musk in 2018. Both are about Tesla cars driving themselves, not about general AI. I found nothing from 2018 where he put a date or a length of time on general AI or superintelligence.

**The two candidates**
- **SXSW, 11 March 2018.** He said self-driving would cover "essentially all modes of driving" and be safer than a person "by the end of next year", which means 2019. The page he spoke from is an *edited* transcript published by an Australian investment firm, Spaceship, not an official one. In that same answer he said "18 months from now", which doesn't quite match the end of 2019. I copied both exactly as printed.
- **Recode Decode with Kara Swisher, recorded 31 October and published 2 November 2018.** He said "we'll get to full self-driving next year". Recode calls its page a "condensed version" of the interview, so you may want to check the full transcript or the recording.

**A judgement call for you:** both are about a Tesla product reaching a level of self-driving. I counted them because they say what an AI system will be able to do by a date. If you treat self-driving forecasts as company plans rather than AI predictions, this year has nothing that qualifies.

**Checked and left out**
- **Joe Rogan, September 2018:** he talks about the singularity and merging with AI but gives no date. His remark that "You can't take 10 years from the point at which it's dangerous" is about how slow regulation is, not about when AI arrives. The transcript page I opened seemed to be only part of the episode.
- **The SXSW AI warnings** ("AI is far more dangerous than nukes", superintelligence as "the single biggest existential crisis") carry no date.
- **Tesla's earnings calls (August and October 2018):** the forward-looking lines were about chips and hardware swaps, mostly spoken by staff, so I left them out as business plans. Both transcripts I opened may be cut short.
- **"Do You Trust This Computer?" (April 2018) and *60 Minutes* (December 2018):** I saw only news coverage of these and didn't open any pages, so I have nothing to quote from them.
